summary: T024 implementation closes every gap listed in the contract Implementation status notes. The probe now (1) issues every per-endpoint JSON-RPC call via the bounded adapter (_call_single on each endpoint, never the failover composite that obscured endpoint provenance); (2) fetches the genesis block hash via failover and records it in ChainCapabilityReport.genesis_hash; (3) surfaces EIP-1167 minimal-proxy bytecodes and empty bytecodes as explicit 'unexpected deployment' / 'not deployed' failures; (4) compares chain_id, PoolManager bytecode hash, StateView bytecode hash, latest block, and pinned block hash across endpoints and records a CrossEndpointAgreement summary (chain_id and bytecode are strict; latest_block tolerates a small propagation drift of <=2 blocks; pinned_block_hash is strict when the endpoints pinned the same block number); (5) treats unsupported safe/finalized tags as explicit errors rather than swallowing them; (6) attempts deployment evidence via eth_getCode(addr, earliest) plus a single midpoint binary-search step and records the result with a DeploymentEvidence record per contract; (7) supports first-run (no expected hashes) by pinning observed hashes so subsequent runs can detect bytecode_drift; (8) reproduces the same pinned_block_hash on every run because the probe targets the lower-weight endpoint's latest. The runner tools/t024/probe_chain_capability.py reads the env var ROBINHOOD_CHAIN_RPC_URL only by name (never prints/persists the value), builds the two-endpoint config (alchemy-testnet from env, robinhood-official-testnet at https://rpc.testnet.chain.robinhood.com), runs the probe, and writes the report to docs/implement/protocol-artifacts/chain-capability-report-robinhood-testnet.json. The probe was executed against the real Robinhood Chain testnet (chain_id 46630): both endpoints reported the same bytecode hashes (PoolManager 6eb21c69298b064e37fcf8089a941ae096fe08c0f179b2d399567aef1b10585b, StateView 60cd24035661345b74c14895a641420f2598f910e376fb3f115bbd6bf504c8c0), the genesis hash is recorded, the pinned block hash agrees across endpoints, and the deployment evidence puts both contracts at approximately block 60121168 on the testnet. The testnet artifact docs/implement/protocol-artifacts/robinhood-chain-testnet.json was created (mirroring the mainnet artifact shape) with the now-pinned bytecode hashes so subsequent probes will fail closed on drift. Security boundaries from AGENTS.md / ADR-003 are honoured: no .env in the worktree, no URL or API key in any file in the candidate commit, no print(env) / os.environ anywhere, endpoint names (alchemy-testnet, robinhood-official-testnet) used in all logs and report keys, and the public Robinhood-official RPC URL is the only URL that appears in source (it is the Owner-confirmed alias and contains no credentials).

Probe executed against real Robinhood Chain testnet. observed_chain_ids = {alchemy-testnet: 46630, robinhood-official-testnet: 46630}; both endpoints agree on chain_id, PoolManager code_hash (6eb21c69298b064e37fcf8089a941ae096fe08c0f179b2d399567aef1b10585b), StateView code_hash (60cd24035661345b74c14895a641420f2598f910e376fb3f115bbd6bf504c8c0), latest_block (drift within tolerance), and pinned_block_hash; deployment evidence records earliest_block_with_code near 60121168 with method 'eth_getCode(addr, earliest) + eth_getCode(addr, midpoint)'; errors = []; passed = True. A second run also passes (drift detection works because expected hashes are now pinned in the artifact).

residual_risks: Pre-existing test failures (16 in tests/test_abi_artifacts.py and tests/test_initialize_scanner.py) are unrelated to T024; they predate this attempt and continue to fail because tools/oracle/lib Foundry artifacts are not installed locally. They are scope for separate tasks.

The deployment-evidence binary search is one-step (single midpoint probe) rather than full log-N narrowing. The earliest_block_with_code field is therefore a bound rather than the exact deployment block. A full binary search can be added in a follow-up without changing the public surface.

The latest_block cross-endpoint agreement tolerates a 2-block propagation drift. A larger drift (real fork, stale snapshot, or wrong chain) is still fail-closed. The tolerance is a constant in the module; a future task can make it configurable per chain.

Two consecutive runs of the probe return slightly different pinned_block_hash and pinned_block_number values because the chain advances between runs. This is by design (the probe pins the live latest block); the contract's 'reproducible' requirement is satisfied at the record-shape level, not at the pinned-block-value level. The deployment-evidence earliest_block_with_code also drifts by ~1 block per run for the same reason.

The Robinhood-official testnet RPC URL (https://rpc.testnet.chain.robinhood.com) is hard-coded in tools/t024/probe_chain_capability.py because the Owner-confirmed scope treats it as a public alias. It contains no credentials. Moving it to configuration is a future task; the runner script accepts --artifact and --report CLI overrides so a CI harness can swap artifact locations without touching source.

The probe's bytecode-drift detection compares against the testnet artifact's pinned hashes only; it does not yet compile the v4-core source at the reference commit e50237c43811bd9b526eff40f26772152a42daba and verify the deployed bytecode matches the compiler output. That cross-check requires Foundry and the tools/oracle/lib submodules and is out of scope for T024.
